REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1, u2, u3, u4
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u4
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, blocker_moved | has_door_key) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, blocker_moved & has_door_key) -> u2
(u1, key_lost) -> u1
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, door_open) -> u3
(u2, key_lost) -> u2
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, target_picked_up) -> u4
(u3, key_lost) -> u3
(u3, else) -> u3
(u4, else) -> u4
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, blocker_moved | has_door_key, u1) -> 0.1
(u1, blocker_moved & has_door_key, u2) -> 0.1
(u2, door_open, u3) -> 0.3
(u3, target_picked_up, u4) -> 1.0
(u1, key_lost, u1) -> -0.1
(u2, key_lost, u2) -> -0.1
(u3, key_lost, u3) -> -0.1
feedback: Accepted. Semantic fidelity: the chain u0 (nothing done) -> u1 (blocker moved or key held) -> u2 (both prerequisites) -> u3 (door open) -> u4 (box carried) matches the task 'open the door and then pick up the box' and the environment-enforced ordering (door_open requires blocker_moved and has_door_key at the toggle step; target_picked_up requires door_open). The u1 conjunction is satisfiable in both orders: ball-first (pick ball, drop aside, pick key) and key-first (pick key, drop fires key_lost, pick ball, pick key), so u2 is reachable. Reachability: when the door first opens while the RM is in u1, the conjunction holds at that same step (agent stands at the ball's former cell holding the key), moving to u2, and the persistent door_open condition delivers u2->u3 (+0.3) the next step, so no milestone is lost. Once unlocked, the door can be reopened without the key, so staying in u3 after a close-shut regression is safe and avoids a re-reward exploit; similarly ignoring blocker_moved regression in u2/u3 is correct because door_open remains achievable. No state can miss target_picked_up: the RM is guaranteed to be in u3 before the agent can cross into the box room. Predicate-only events: uses only the five given propositions, no invented predicates. Persistent/event distinction: key_lost is correctly treated as a one-step event with -0.1 self-loop penalties in exactly the states where it can fire (u1, u2, u3; it cannot fire in u0 because any has_door_key step exits u0, and u4 terminates the episode); drops while the door is open (e.g., step 19 of the trace) fall to the else-loop with no penalty, matching the event definition. Ordered transition coverage and else coverage: every state has a catch-all else self-loop covering irrelevant or regressive events (door toggled shut in u3, ball re-dropped in front in u1/u2/u3, no-op turns/moves), and labels within each state are mutually exclusive given the environment's exclusivity constraints (key_lost vs has_door_key, key_lost vs door_open, key_lost vs target_picked_up). Reward safety: progress rewards 0.1/0.1/0.3/1.0 are dense across milestones and bounded (max 1.5); absorbing progress states prevent re-reward farming; the small -0.1 penalty appropriately implements the soft 'try not to drop the key while the door is still closed' constraint, including the forced drop in the key-first path. Note the u3 penalty also fires if the key is dropped after an open-close cycle, which is consistent with the event's formal truth condition (door closed at the drop step). Compactness: 5 states is minimal for remembering 'at least one prerequisite seen' before requiring the conjunction. Format: FINAL_STATES header present and nonempty (u4), declared in STATES, and accepting for the task (box picked up); reward entries correspond one-to-one with declared transitions. Minor note only: the disjunction label 'blocker_moved | has_door_key' is a shorthand for two same-reward transitions and is semantically unambiguous here since the two propositions cannot co-occur in u0.

All five environment-declared propositions are defined exactly once; no undeclared extras, no imports, actions, or side effects, and nothing mutates env or episode memory.

- blocker_moved: scans the grid for the unique door and tests the cell left of it for a ball. With one door at (dx, dy) and the blocker cell at (dx-1, dy) per _gen_grid, this reduces exactly to the required reading: false iff a ball sits on (dx-1, dy); a ball in hand is off-grid so it counts as moved, and dropping the ball back there turns it false again. The x > 0 guard only prevents get(-1, y); even hypothetically it cannot change the result since get out of bounds returns None. Syntax of the nested generator (inner any referencing outer x via closure, short-circuited by the and-chain) is valid.
- has_door_key: identical to the documented expression (carrying a key whose color matches the door's color), no extra lock/open condition.
- door_open: identical to the documented expression, a pure current-state reading of is_open.
- target_picked_up: identical to the documented expression, matching the box named by env.mission rather than a fixed color.
- key_lost: correct event semantics - prev['has_door_key'] and not K and not D, with K and D inlined with expressions identical to the persistent functions and compared against the read-only previous_valuation snapshot. The extra truthiness guard on previous_valuation is harmless (it is always a complete non-empty valuation, all-false at step 1, which already forces key_lost false), and bool() only normalizes the return type. Read-only; no mutation.

Only documented API is used (env.grid.get with None guards, env.carrying, env.mission, env.width/height, env.episode_memory['previous_valuation'], object type/color/is_open). The example trace reproduces: step 4 blocker_moved true, step 12 has_door_key true, step 17 door_open true, step 19 drop leaves key_lost false because the door is open (not D fails), step 28 target_picked_up true; the key-first alternative fires key_lost exactly one step on the drop while the door is closed. Constraints (door_open after blocker_moved and has_door_key, key_lost mutually exclusive with has_door_key, door_open, and target_picked_up) all follow from these expressions.
